summary: The Minnesota Wild fired head coach Dean Evason and assistant Bob Woods on a Monday in November 2023, with John Hynes reported as the replacement. The article reviews Evason's coaching career and the Wild's best-ever 2021-22 season, then explains the team's 5-10-4 start, driven by injuries, poor goaltending, and a struggling Kirill Kaprizov. It also covers Hynes's contract situation with Nashville and the challenges of the competitive Central Division.
one_line: The Wild fired coach Dean Evason and assistant Bob Woods after a 5-10-4 start, reportedly hiring John Hynes as his replacement.
key_facts: The Minnesota Wild relieved head coach Dean Evason and assistant coach Bob Woods of their duties effective immediately, per a Monday evening statement.
The Athletic's Michael Russo reported the Wild will name former Devils and Predators coach John Hynes as Evason's successor.
Evason joined the Wild organization as an assistant in 2018; Woods joined the bench one season earlier.

Evason, 59, began coaching with the WHL's Calgary Hitmen in 1998-99, and his first NHL job was as a Capitals assistant after the 2004-05 lockout, where he coached Alex Ovechkin for his first seven NHL seasons.
From 2012 Evason coached the Predators' AHL affiliate, the Milwaukee Admirals, and was promoted to Wild head coach when Bruce Boudreau was fired late in the 2019-20 season.
In 2021-22 the Wild won more than 50 games for the first time since 2000 and earned 113 points, but lost in the first round to the 109-point Blues.
The Wild have no playoff series win since 2015 and no Conference Final appearance since 2002-03.
At the time of the firing, the Wild were 5-10-4, winless in seven straight and without a win since Nov. 7 against the Islanders.
Captain Jared Spurgeon missed the first 13 games, and Filip Gustavsson and Marc-André Fleury have a combined .878 SV%, near the league bottom.
Kirill Kaprizov is on pace for a career-low 26 goals and has a team-worst -10 rating.
Hynes was let go by the Predators after last season but is in the final year of his Nashville contract, so he will be paid by both Minnesota and Nashville this season.
The Wild's penalty kill is league-worst at 66.7%, while Nashville's was tied for fourth last season at 82.6%.
The Wild remain on the hook for Evason's contract through 2024-25 at just under $2M per season.
